task: S1 — arm S against arm A on ADR-061 (6)'s paired per-block sign criterion
criterion: over 14 spatial blocks under FULL leave-fold-out CV, count the blocks where arm S is CLOSER to truth's stage_decay than arm A. BAR >= 11/14 (exact one-sided p = 0.0287). Fixed in ADR-061 (6); not re-derived here.

interpretation_limit.citation: ADR-062 (3), declared before this number existed
interpretation_limit.if_the_bar_clears: a count >= 11/14 establishes that arm S lands CLOSER TO TRUTH PER BLOCK than arm A on stage_decay. It establishes NOTHING about structure. It may NOT be described as the model having learned fire stage.
interpretation_limit.why: arm S decelerates everywhere, so it lands closer on the decelerating blocks and further on the accelerating ones. A uniform shift in a useful direction can clear a per-block closeness count without reproducing any structure at all. The quantity that speaks to structure is SIGN AGREEMENT with truth, reported here and adjudicating nothing.
interpretation_limit.non_adjudicating: `stage_decay` is NOT a licensed gate criterion (C6.6 [v2.15]); `eval.stage.licence()` is called on every run of this script and returns NOT_LICENSED. This artifact is therefore a per-block COMPARISON, not a gate.

cv_matrix.why_members_are_cells_not_folds: C8.1's count clause exists so a fold that silently does not exist cannot move the denominator of a >= 11/14 count. Declaring one member per CELL (fold x arm) checks the same property for every run that contributed a number, which is strictly more than declaring five. The cost is that `cv_matrix_members_distinct` REPORTS duplicates: 15 members carry 5 fingerprints, three cells per fold by design. That clause is REPORTING precisely for this case (the null rung IS the same split twice, ADR-062 (4)) and the artifact says which it is, as the clause asks.
expected_reporting_flags: C8.1.cv_matrix_members_distinct — 15 members, 5 distinct fingerprints, 3 cells per fold (arm A seed 1, arm S seed 1, arm A seed 2). By design, not a defect.

wall_clock.note: the matrix only; the arm-A bitwise identity control (~9 min) and the aggregation are not in it

cost_gate.caveat: folds 0 and 1 have the largest train sets by hours x cells (0.04e9 vs 0.03e9), so their trainings are up to ~15% dearer than the measured fold-3 pair. The projection uses the measured mean and does not include that uplift.

null_rung_proposal.adopted: RETRAIN arm A at seed 2 on every fold and run the identical scoring and the identical per-block sign computation with arm S replaced by arm A(seed 2). Cost: 5 extra trainings + 1 extra full scoring pass (~40 min + ~9 min measured).
null_rung_proposal.why: The criterion compares two INDEPENDENTLY FITTED arms, so its null distribution has to contain optimisation noise. Retraining is the only perturbation whose ONLY difference from the real comparison is which of the two models carries the stage head.
null_rung_proposal.rejected_cheaper_option: Re-score ONE arm-A checkpoint at a different `predict` seed and call that arm A vs arm A. It costs one scoring pass and no training, and it is INVALID: both sides are the same fit, so it measures only 24-member Monte-Carlo noise, is centred at 7/14 by construction and essentially cannot leave the [4,10] band. A control that cannot fail is not a control — the same defect as ADR-060 (3)'s closure identity, where a 1%-effective arm scored what a perfect arm scored.
null_rung_proposal.reported_alongside: The inference-seed comparison is worth reporting anyway as a NOISE FLOOR, since it separates 'the ensemble is noisy' from 'the fit is noisy'. It is not the rung.

licence.registry_refusal: 'stage_decay' is not in C6_METRICS, so nothing has ruled on whether it may decide the S1 arm comparison. An unregistered metric is an unchecked metric; register it with a direction and a gate_eligible flag before letting it decide anything.

verdict: arm S is closer to truth on 13/14 blocks (one-sided p = 0.0009); the bar is 11/14. PASSES. Null rung 6/14 — in band. LIMIT (ADR-062 (3)): this is closeness per block and says NOTHING about structure.
